source_review.notes: Checked all eight references for identity, publication context, and cited scope. Fowler's revised 2024 Continuous Integration article supports rapid feedback and staged builds. Google SRE Testing for Reliability and Release Engineering chapters support short feedback cycles, exact release subjects, complete gate targets, and coverage-versus-cadence reasoning. Google Test Sizes supports observable resource constraints, isolation, and parallelization. Elbaum, Malishevsky, and Rothermel IEEE TSE 2002 supports the definition and empirical evaluation of test-case prioritization for rate of fault detection. Current Google Engineering Practices supports small self-contained changes; current Bazel remote-cache documentation supports cache operation and warns about invalid uploads when build inputs mutate. Verified Humble and Farley bibliographic metadata and pipeline scope. Current documentation retrieved 2026-09-06.

evidence: Defined queue, setup, execution, reporting, path, vertex-duration, sequential-duration, conditional-failure, required-claim, and evidence-set notation before use.
Checked all sums, products, expectations, set inclusion, set membership, maximum path, nonnegative and probability domains, subscripts, and GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The sequential ordering model is explicitly conditional on deterministic durations and stable conditional probabilities.

evidence: Executed feedback-ordering-model under CPython 3.14.4 and matched seven exact output lines with empty stderr and exit status zero.
Recomputed expected duration as 2 + 0.70(4) + 0.70(0.80)(8) + 0.70(0.80)(0.75)(20) = 17.68 and all-pass duration as 34.
Recomputed worked example 2 as 3+0.85(12)=13.2 versus 12+0.70(3)=14.1, and exercise 2 as 5+0.60(2)+0.60(0.90)(10)=11.6 with all-pass duration 17.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Times and probabilities are illustrative model values, not measured repository or industry performance.

evidence: Derived the sequential expected time by multiplying each duration by the probability its check is reached.
Expanded two-check expected orders, subtracted them, and verified the pairwise condition p_a d_b >= p_b d_a is equivalent to descending p/d for positive durations.
Checked the weighted longest dependency path lower-bounds ideal workflow completion when predecessor constraints hold.
Checked admission requires required claims to be a subset of claims backed by valid completed evidence.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The adjacent-exchange ordering result is bounded to the stated model and not asserted for correlated, severity-weighted, resource-constrained workflows.

evidence: Reviewed first-signal versus complete-decision endpoints; queue, setup, execution, reporting, and human-response intervals; passing, failing, cancelled, superseded, unstable, unavailable, and infrastructure-lost runs.

Reviewed no cache, stale and poisoned cache, incomplete keys, mutable inputs, clean builds, incremental hidden dependencies, selector ambiguity, generated inputs, mandatory high-impact suites, periodic full runs, and random holdouts.

Reviewed serial and parallel graphs, critical and off-path work, load saturation, shared external bottlenecks, static and dynamic shards, stragglers, duplicate execution, cancellation delay, and diagnostic retention.

Reviewed rare severe defects, biased historical failure data, small high-impact changes, emergency waivers, deferred exposure, rollback containment, p50/p95/p99 divergence, and metric-denominator manipulation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter treats evidence loss and deferred exposure as policy changes rather than latency improvements.

evidence: Traced every latency claim to an explicit start, end, subject, evidence class, consumer, and population.
Checked prioritization preserves all required checks for a passing candidate while selection and deferral alter the evidence set and require separate authority.
Checked every reused result binds declared source, dependency, toolchain, flag, platform, environment, trust, and policy inputs.
Checked skipped, deferred, cancelled, unavailable, unstable, and selected-away evidence never silently enters the completed-evidence set.
Checked optimizer measurement retains unsuccessful and censored candidates and pairs speed with detection, escape, invalidation, compute, and diagnostic measures.
invariant_checking.notes: Speed, assurance, and cost remain separate quantities throughout.

evidence: Reviewed the pairwise interchange proof, including conditional reach probability and division only by positive durations.
Reviewed coverage preservation and confirmed it applies to reordered checks for passing candidates, not selected or deferred checks.
Reviewed the critical-path lower-bound argument and its explicit exclusion of queueing and resource contention.
Reviewed the anti-gaming argument and confirmed excluding slow failed, cancelled, or lost runs changes the population rather than improving experience.
proof_review.notes: No theorem is generalized beyond its assumptions; empirical prioritization research is not presented as proof of universal benefit.

evidence: Audited uses of optimal, sound, safe, complete, required, pass, failure, probability, proves, verifies, critical, equivalent, and improvement.
Confirmed mathematical model results, historical empirical findings, current documentation behavior, professional design judgment, hypothetical cases, and local execution evidence are distinguished.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter repeatedly states that historical probabilities, cache identity, and selector mappings are conditional evidence rather than guarantees.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet under CPython 3.14.4 with declared exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit status zero.

Confirmed ratio ordering, expected stop time, passing-candidate total, non-omission under prioritization, non-equivalence of sampling and complete evidence, cache-hit limitation, and required-claim inclusion.
Confirmed all dashboard, scheduling, sharding, cache, selector, migration, cancellation, tail, and incentive cases are hypothetical teaching situations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real CI service, repository history, build, test suite, runner fleet, queue, cache, selector, escaped defect, or production deployment was measured.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the complete chain from feedback contracts and latency decomposition through demand reduction, information ordering, dependency critical paths, sharding, cache identity, incremental validity, selection envelopes, explicit lanes, fail-fast semantics, test improvement, and multidimensional evaluation. First signal, full gate decision, compute cost, and assurance remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed operational failures across hidden queues, weak endpoints, redundant builds, biased ordering, capacity saturation, straggler shards, stale caches, mutable build inputs, hidden dependencies, selector ambiguity, mandatory risks, post-merge deferral, emergency waivers, cancellation, retry erasure, infrastructure loss, slow fixtures, narrow versus end-to-end coverage, tail latency, survivorship bias, and incentive gaming. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified undergraduate progression from precise latency and evidence vocabulary through four equations, four bounded arguments, one executable seven-outcome scheduling model, eight trade-off pairs, eighteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked situations, and five exercises progressing from definitions through derivation, critical-path diagnosis, selector design, and organizational incentive transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Textbooks, articles, current documentation, a deterministic scheduling model, and hypothetical cases do not establish any real failure probability, selector soundness, cache correctness, test adequacy, queue behavior, escaped-defect rate, developer productivity, CI cost, or production risk.
